justification: Changes which quotes count as proven; a dry-run tool, writes only with --apply and a backup. Not critical: the DB trigger still holds any unproven row.

pre_impl.existing_data: dcp_setback_controls.quote_status column, read and stamped by this checker
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: A quote wholly on the next page was marked verbatim; now wrong_page (24 rows in dry run)
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Existing rows only when the checker is re-run with --apply

functions.name: _spans
functions.output: True only if the match starts on page a and ends on page b
functions.if_none: callers pass strings only; empty quote returns no_source before this

functions.name: classify
functions.input: quote text, list of chapter page texts, cited pdf_page number
functions.output: one of verbatim, wrong_page, not_found, no_source
functions.if_none: returns no_source so the row stays held

break_it.scenario: Quote wholly on the next page marked verbatim
break_it.what_happens: a rule shown with the wrong page cited
break_it.how: scripts/dcp_quote_status.py _spans requires the match to cross the break

break_it.scenario: Quote sitting entirely on the earlier page while pdf_page points one page later
break_it.what_happens: the reader is sent one page past where the council text actually is
break_it.how: same _spans check for the i-1 pair

break_it.scenario: Genuine quote split over the break rejected
break_it.what_happens: a correct council rule would be hidden from the page
break_it.how: _spans accepts a match starting in a and ending in b

falsifiable_check.fails_when: classify still returns verbatim for a quote wholly on pdf_page+1 or pdf_page-1
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Before the fix, test_quote_wholly_on_the_next_page_is_wrong_page returned verbatim (red); dry run on live data flagged 24 rows
